request: We've built a reporting add-on for our existing B2B product and want a go-to-market plan for selling it into a customer segment we've never targeted before.

objective.value: Win paying customers for the reporting add-on in a new customer segment. The target number and the clock are not stated.
objective.evidence: Client: "a go-to-market plan for selling it into a customer segment we've never targeted before." The outcome (revenue, pilots, logos) is deduced, not stated.

success_metric.evidence: Nothing stated about a leading indicator or what it should exclude (e.g. free pilots, existing customers adding the add-on).

icp.value: A segment is chosen but not named. It is new to the company, so there is no customer history in it.
icp.evidence: Client: "a customer segment we've never targeted before." No firmographics, buyer role or exclusions given.

existing_distribution.value: An installed base of the existing B2B product probably exists. It was gathered for a different segment and promise, so it may not match the new ICP. Any audience, partner or community in the new segment is unknown.
existing_distribution.evidence: Client: "our existing B2B product" and "never targeted before." Whether any relationship reaches the new segment is not stated.

claims.text: An installed base of the existing product exists.
No audience or relationship exists in the new segment.

offer.value: A reporting add-on built on the existing product. It is unclear whether the new segment must also adopt the base product, which would make this a two-part purchase. Pricing, packaging and trial terms are unknown.
offer.evidence: Client: "a reporting add-on for our existing B2B product." Whether it is sold standalone is not stated.

objections.value: Likely objections in an unfamiliar segment: trust, data handling, switching cost, and the need to adopt the base product. None is confirmed.
objections.evidence: Not discussed. Reporting often pulls sensitive figures into a new place, which raises the impact of this slot.
objections.test_plan: Run 8-10 discovery calls with people in the target segment and ask what would stop them buying. Record the objections that recur.

alternatives.evidence: What the segment uses today (spreadsheets, BI tools, a competitor) and what it costs them is unknown. Impact is raised because the add-on will be priced and the price anchor depends on this.

channels.evidence: No channels discussed. Impact is raised because there is no known distribution in the segment, and the segment may bring a regulated audience or contact rules.

unit_economics.evidence: No price, margin, expected customer lifetime or acceptable acquisition cost stated.

capacity.evidence: Hours per week and number of weeks available for go-to-market work, and who does it, are not stated. This is the binding constraint on the plan.

budget.evidence: No budget stated, and no indication whether it is committed or conditional on early results.

horizon.evidence: No date or review point stated.

instrumentation.evidence: Nothing stated. Low priority until the metric and channels are set.

decision_thresholds.evidence: No rule stated for when to continue, change or stop the effort in the new segment.

questions.q: How many hours per week can your team actually give to this go-to-market effort, for how many weeks, and who is doing the work?
questions.why: High impact and fully unknown. A plan that does not fit the hours available is not a plan, and this sets how many channels we can consider.

questions.q: Which segment is it, and who is the buyer inside it? Can you also name a type of company in that segment that the add-on is not for?
questions.why: The whole plan depends on it, and a segment you have never sold to has no history to guess from. If it is regulated, the channel and offer options change.

questions.q: What do you already have that reaches this segment: customers who sit in or near it, partners, a community, an email list, or anyone who knows you there? Or is it a cold start?
questions.why: This decides which channels are viable at all. Proposing channels before knowing it would mean designing on an unknown.

questions.q: Does a buyer in the new segment need your base product to use the add-on, or can they buy it on its own? And if it needs the base product, is the plan to sell both together?
questions.why: This changes the sales effort from an upsell to a full product sale, which affects price, objections and the time it takes to close.

questions.q: What is the one result you want from this, and by when? For example, a number of paying customers or a revenue figure within six months.
questions.why: Without a target and a date there is no success metric and no point at which to continue, change or stop.

summary.objective: Sell the reporting add-on to a new customer segment the company has never targeted. The target and the date are not yet defined.
summary.scope: A go-to-market plan covering the segment and buyer, the offer and pricing, the channels, the objections to answer, and the measures and thresholds for deciding whether to continue. The scope is sized to the team's available hours once those are known.
assumptions: An installed base of the existing product exists, but it was gathered for a different segment and may not reach the new one.
The add-on is sold alongside or on top of the base product. Whether it can be bought standalone is unconfirmed.
Buyers' main objections are trust, data handling and the effort of adopting the base product. This needs to be tested in conversations with the segment.
Nothing is known yet about the segment's current alternatives, willingness to pay, budget or timeline.
summary.blind_spot: Team hours and existing reach into the new segment are both unknown. A plan built on channels before those are answered would probably assume more hands and more audience than exist. A related risk is that the segment may have to adopt the base product to use the add-on, which turns an upsell into a full product sale.

objective.value: Win first customers for the reporting add-on in a new customer segment (not yet targeted). Target outcome and date not stated.
objective.evidence: Client: 'we want a go-to-market plan for selling it into a customer segment we've never targeted before.'

unit_economics.test_plan: Run a pricing and willingness-to-pay test with 5-10 segment prospects, then derive the CAC and payback thresholds from the quoted price and sales cycle.

questions.why: uncertainty × impact: every other choice (channels, offer, objections, alternatives) depends on it, and it is currently unnamed.

questions.why: uncertainty × impact: this is the binding constraint, and a plan that exceeds the available hours is not a plan.

questions.why: uncertainty × impact: without a target and a clock, no threshold or budget can be derived.

questions.why: uncertainty × impact: your reporting handles sensitive financial data, so the objection and the incumbent define positioning and price.

summary.objective: Build a go-to-market plan to sell the reporting add-on into a customer segment the company has never targeted, with no target or date yet defined.
summary.scope: Likely scope: define the segment and buyer, position the add-on against what they use today, choose a few channels the available hours can support, set a price and offer, and define success measures and stop/continue thresholds. Details are open until the segment and capacity are known.
assumptions: The new segment has no existing relationship with the company, so distribution must be built from scratch.
The add-on probably depends on the core product, which may make the offer a two-step adoption.
Reporting touches sensitive financial data, so trust and auditability are likely the main objections.
Budget, hours and timeline are unknown and not assumed.
summary.blind_spot: The team's available selling hours and any existing foothold in the new segment: both decide which channels are viable, and the plan cannot be sized until they are known.

summary.objective: Build a go-to-market plan to sell the reporting add-on into a customer segment the company has never targeted. The success target and deadline are not yet defined.
summary.scope: Likely scope: define the segment and the offer, identify the reachable channels given available people and distribution, and set success metrics and decision thresholds. Out of scope for now: product changes to the add-on.
assumptions: The existing customer base does not match the new segment, so there is little or no direct reach.
The add-on sits on top of the existing product, so the new segment may need to adopt the core product too (to confirm).
A buyer in the new segment will need proof of trust and data handling before switching (to test in buyer conversations).
A pricing model and willingness to pay in the new segment are unknown and will need to be tested.
